sources.entry: Helium - Color-coded student planner for classes, homework, grades, and notes with smart notifications and multi-device sync. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: Helium platform is the open-source backend (Django API and worker) for the Helium color-coded online student planner covering classes, homework, grades, and notes.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the backend "platform" for Helium, a student planner, including its API and a worker process for async and scheduled tasks. It is written in Python with Django and organized into the apps auth, common, feed, importexport, and planner, with configuration under conf. The README describes a Docker-based development setup that starts separate API and worker containers, plus a LocalStack container to emulate AWS services locally. Environment variables control the hostname mode (dev-local, local, prod), AWS Secrets Manager use, and ngrok tunneling for local runserver use. Tests run via make test with a coverage report, and auto-generated API documentation is served at /docs. The frontend lives in a separate repository.
use_cases: Running a self-hosted student planner backend
Developing or contributing to the Helium planner API
Tracking classes, homework, and grades in a planner app
Integrating third-party clients with a student planner API
Running async and scheduled notification tasks for a planner
how_to_run: Install Docker, Python (>= 3.12), MySQL (>= 8), and Redis (>= 7)
Run `make` to build and start the API and worker containers
Create an admin user with `docker exec -it platform-api-1 python manage.py createsuperuser`
Open a shell in a container with `docker exec -it platform-api-1 /bin/bash`
notable: Split into API and worker containers for async and scheduled tasks
Local development uses LocalStack to emulate AWS services offline
Environment modes switch hostnames between localhost and prod-like domains
Released container images published to AWS ECR
caveats: Frontend is in a separate repository, so the full app needs both repos
Some features such as email and text messages need Internet-connected third-party services and Terraform workspace setup
Default Docker image targets linux/arm64; x86 users must set PLATFORM=amd64
